p1_findings.title: Runner does not bind the exact independently reviewed CPU-preflight receipt and outer-seal identities before consuming the one-shot
evidence: The M670 request freezes preflight.json SHA 8dbab013... and SHA256SUMS.seal.sha256 file SHA adbc9600... as review roots.
Runner lines 45-56 require external runner and contract SHA roots only.

Runner lines 186-208 verify that the preflight is internally double-sealed and satisfies status, contract-SHA, parameter-name and load-count predicates, but never compare either preflight file to the two identities frozen by M670.

The independent private-copy attack changed preflight.json, regenerated both seals, produced different receipt and outer-seal-file SHAs, and still passed every literal preflight predicate used by the runner.
Runner creates the attempt directory immediately afterward at line 211.
p1_findings.impact: A reviewed preflight can be replaced after review by a different consistently resealed receipt that preserves the small semantic subset checked by the runner. The producer may later detect a real topology fault, but the scarce one-shot has already been consumed. This violates the request's exact-preflight and independently reviewed identity boundary.
minimum_repair: Require two nonempty reviewer-supplied values before resource checks: M660R2_EXPECTED_PREFLIGHT_RECEIPT_SHA256 and M660R2_EXPECTED_PREFLIGHT_OUTER_SEAL_SHA256.
After nested-seal verification and again immediately before mkdir(attempt), compare preflight.json and SHA256SUMS.seal.sha256 file digests to those values.
Record both expected and observed identities in the initial attempt receipt and identity manifest.

Because changing the runner changes the contract input identity and therefore the contract SHA, regenerate the CPU exact-load preflight against the repaired contract, freeze the new receipt and outer-seal identities, and request a fresh independent review.

decision.reason: M670 requires P0=0 and P1=0; this review has P1=1.
